title: How a seam should feel
excerpt: If you can feel the seam more than the cloth, the garment is already arguing with you.
author: Mara Ellison

blocks.text: A good seam disappears into the cloth. You notice it only when you look for it: even stitches, a clean fold, no ridge against the skin.
Felled, not faked
On a work shirt we fell the side seam so the raw edge never touches you. It takes more cloth and more time. It also lasts.
Repair starts at the seam. If the stitch is honest, a tailor can open it and close it again.
What to run a thumb along

items: Shoulder: it should sit, not bite
Side: no twist after a wash

title: Washing wool without fear
excerpt: Wool is not porcelain. It is hair. Treat it like hair and it will last.
author: Jonah Peck

blocks.text: Most wool dies in a hot spin, not in the rain. Cold water, a little soap, a towel, a flat table. That is the whole ritual.
Dry it flat
Hanging a wet pullover grows the body and shrinks the sleeve. Lay it out. Shape the shoulder with your hands. Walk away.
When to dry clean
Tailored trousers and the overcoat. Not the merino mockneck. Not the scarf. Save the solvent for structure.

items: Steam creases, do not iron wool dry

title: A note on fit and ease
excerpt: Ease is the air between you and the cloth. Too little and you cannot sit. Too much and the garment has no job.
author: Priya Shah

blocks.text: We cut some things close — the mockneck, the column — and some things with room. The oversized sweatshirt is not a mistake. It is a jacket you can wash.
Size for the job
If you layer a pullover under the overcoat, take the coat in your usual size. Oak & Thread cut it for that. If you wear the denim jacket over a heavy knit, size up.
Fit is not a number. It is whether you can raise an arm without the hem climbing.

items: Check the back rise, not only the waist

title: Linen in a city summer
excerpt: Linen wrinkles. That is the cloth telling the truth about heat. Stop chasing a crease that will return in an hour.
author: Elena Voss

blocks.text: We wash the camp shirt so the first wrinkle is already there. You are not failing the garment when it creases on the train.
Hang it, do not fight it
A steam at the collar is enough. The body can stay soft. Ivory linen is a little sheer; Sage is the safer day shirt.
What we wear with it

items: Nothing else that tries to be sharp

title: Why we repair first
excerpt: Atelier Vale is a shop, not a landfill. A broken stitch is a morning. A new coat is a season of cloth.
author: Ruth Calder

blocks.text: Broadway keeps a machine in the back. Valencia has a cobbler two doors down for the derby. We would rather take a hem up than sell you a second pair of trousers you do not need.
What we will do

items: Restitch a popped seam on house garments
Point you to a cobbler for the derby
Replace a buckle if ours fails

blocks.text: What we will not do
We will not pretend a glued sole is a feature. We will not print a fake live-visitor count on the product page. The stock number is the stock number.
Clothes that stay sharp are clothes that can be opened and closed again.

title: Layering without bulk
excerpt: The trick is one thin warm thing and one structured thing. Not three fleeces.
author: Theo March

blocks.text: Merino mockneck, then the work shirt, then the overcoat. That is a January commute. The pullover replaces the shirt, it does not sit under it.
Collars
Two collars is enough. The mockneck is a collar. The shirt is a collar. Leave the coat open if you want air.

items: Cloth with a seam in the middle

title: Denim that is allowed to fade
excerpt: A rinse is not a finish line. It is a starting colour. The rest is your year.
author: Samir Cole

blocks.text: Oak & Thread rinse the slim jacket once so you do not spend six months looking like a raw-denim poster. After that, the creases are yours.
Wash rare
Cold, inside-out, hang. Spot-clean the cuffs. The Sand colour will lighten at the elbow. That is not damage.
If you want it to stay dark, buy Ink and wash it even less.
Kids denim
The kids pair has a doubled knee because slides are not a style choice. Wash those more. They earn it.
